trigger: a reader relies on the README Windows Measured cell at HEAD, which says every commit after the last code-bearing rig run changes comments, docs and generated JSON only
classification_rationale: a verification-scope claim in operator-facing docs that this range makes false: the range moves compiled code
summary: The Windows Measured note said later commits change comments, docs and generated JSON only, but this range moves compiled code. Reported independently by enterprise-readiness (ER-1), plugin-developer (pd-1), docs-writer (docs-writer-3) and consistency-auditor (cons-1) (4). fixed in dc7a748be: the note scopes the rig run to the commit before the lift and names the lift's own verification (kingsley, native MSVC, elevated, 107 cases / 1,259 assertions); the plugin-docs JSON is regenerated and plugin_doc_gen --check reports 0 errors.

trigger: a pre-commit clang-format run (the CI lint job is disabled)
classification_rationale: ColumnLimit 100 on lines this range added: privacy_permissions_win.cpp:28 (132 columns) and win_hive_file_probe.hpp:9-10 (102, 104), plus a double blank line at privacy_permissions_win.cpp:108-109
summary: Three added comment lines exceeded the column limit, one of them left by the commit that was meant to fix this. fixed in dc7a748be: the blocks are re-wrapped by hand and the double blank line removed; a code-point measure over base..head finds no added C++ line over 100 columns.

trigger: a reviewer reads the banner as fleet-wide guard coverage
classification_rationale: the banner said the guard is shared by every plugin that mounts a profile hive, but five other with_user_hive callers pass no OfflineHiveFileCheck and only privacy_permissions passes it; lines 15-17 already disclosed opt-in, so this is not a false-assurance (I6a) case
summary: The guard header overstated how widely it is used. Reported independently by docs-writer (docs-writer-2), architect (arch-3) and consistency-auditor (cons-3) (3); security-guardian found no contradiction in the opt-in claims. fixed in dc7a748be: the banner says the guard is meant for any such plugin, that today only privacy_permissions' read arm passes it, and that the default-on work is tracked in #5291.

trigger: a reader trusts 'each method mirrors one Win32 call' when judging the raw-code seam
classification_rationale: leaf_facts makes eight Win32 calls; the comment moved verbatim from the plugin
summary: The HiveFileProbe comment said each method mirrors one Win32 call. fixed in dc7a748be: each method answers one probe question, the stated reason for raw codes is narrowed to keeping the seam to one shape plus the partial listing list_sidecars returns, and one probe instance is documented as serving one hive load on one thread (the cpp-safety observation that `opens` is not atomic).

trigger: a reader of the moved comments
classification_rationale: the probe banner's relative clause attached the sidecar own-handle re-read to the listing; the plugin TU comment mixed repo-relative and bare header names; the using-directive note was terse; the internals test header wrapped raggedly
summary: Four small wording defects in comments the lift added or touched. fixed in dc7a748be.

trigger: a reader follows e330f2592 / 3d4f0e738 cited in the message of 9979c5107
classification_rationale: the cited commits exist only on a local branch of the earlier cut of the same change; history is never rewritten
summary: One commit message cites SHAs that are not in this history. The change itself is self-contained. fixed by giving the provenance in the PR description (the cited commits are the earlier local cut of the same change); no history rewrite.

trigger: a later name present in both yuzu and yuzu::win, or a consumer that adds `using namespace yuzu::privacy_permissions::win`
classification_rationale: the only namespace-scope using-directive in any agents/ header; the re-export idiom is named using-declarations (browser_inventory_parsers.hpp:90-91); cpp-expert verified an 18-declaration replacement with -fsyntax-only under the project flags
summary: The plugin re-exports yuzu::win with a using-directive in a header, and four of the .cpp using-declarations are read only by the TU-inclusion test. Reported independently by cpp-expert (cpp-expert-1), consistency-auditor (cons-2) and cross-platform (cross-platform-1) (3). Kept in this range as the minimal-diff glue of a pure move (no code edit, so the Mac, MSVC and lane evidence stands); linked to #5291, to be replaced by named using-declarations, with the four test-only aliases moved into the test, when the guard API is settled for its next consumer.

trigger: a translation unit with both `using namespace yuzu;` and `using namespace yuzu::privacy_permissions;` that names `win::`
classification_rationale: yuzu::win was Windows-only; the pure guard header now creates it on every host; reproduced on Apple clang (base compiles, head fails); no such translation unit exists today
summary: The pure guard header introduces namespace yuzu::win on POSIX hosts, which makes `win` ambiguous in a TU holding both using-directives. Linked to #5291: decide the namespace or an alias when the next consumer adopts the guard.

trigger: a second consumer initialises HiveFileGuard without `snapshot` or `expired`, reuses one guard across profiles, passes an empty profile_sid, or wires only before_load
classification_rationale: the guard is a positional aggregate whose hook pairing is a prose contract; the sole consumer (privacy_permissions_win.cpp:258-266) wires it correctly and an empty `expired` throws before any syscall (fails closed), so the wrong outcome cannot occur in production today (E6)
summary: HiveFileGuard's shape invites misuse by a second consumer. Reported independently by cpp-expert (cpp-expert-2), unhappy-path (UP-1) and architect (arch-1) (3). Linked to #5291, which already carries the deferred constructor-shape decision (g5293-cl8); suggested shape: required constructor arguments, a `snapshot{}` default, and a factory returning the complete OfflineHiveFileCheck so a before-only wiring is unrepresentable.

trigger: a second consumer includes the shared headers
classification_rationale: the narrow yuzu::win::UniqueHandle claims a generic name among six handle owners in the tree, and shared coverage is carried by plugin-named tests (precedent: test_<header>.cpp)
summary: Naming and test-placement debts of promoting a plugin-private owner to a shared header. Linked to #5291: address when the second consumer adopts the headers.

trigger: a reader loads the first of the duplicated rows
classification_rationale: the browser_inventory and privacy_permissions rows each appear twice and the copies diverge in clause (6) (also on origin/dev); this range edited both copies identically
summary: Duplicated, diverged routed-concern rows. Noted by docs-writer, architect (arch-3) and consistency-auditor (cons-4) (3). Linked to #5291: the change that next edits the privacy_permissions row (the second consumer's) collapses the duplicates; a docs-only cleanup is not raised separately.

trigger: a later edit deletes failure_code's GEN_FAILURE mapping, the ERROR_MORE_DATA sizing branch or the listing limit and the suite stays green; or a 256-259 character path reaches the probe
classification_rationale: three branches and a long-path shape have no assertion (none at base either); the guard's fake-probe tests pin the guard side
summary: Unpinned branches of the Windows probe shell. Reported by quality-engineer (quality-engineer-1) and unhappy-path (UP-2) (2); both read the code as correct and fail-closed. Linked to #5291: add CHECK(failure_code(0) == ERROR_GEN_FAILURE), a limit+5 sidecar listing case and a 257-character path through the real probe on kingsley before the second consumer relies on the probe.

trigger: a move constructor is added to UniqueHandle
classification_rationale: the new doc says the owner is neither copyable nor movable; the internals test asserts only !is_copy_constructible_v; cpp-safety verified the claim (the deleted copy constructor suppresses the implicit move)
summary: The non-movable claim is true but only half pinned. Linked to #5291 with the probe test pins: one added `!std::is_move_constructible_v<UniqueHandle>` assertion.

classification_rationale: the README-touch rule keys on agents/plugins/<x>/src/; the moved code is outside it; review routing survives because the routed row names both headers
summary: The plugin README-touch check does not follow code that moves to agents/shared. Deferred to a new issue covering path-keyed checks that no longer see the relocated guard (this and the CodeQL spawn queries).

trigger: a future edit adds a non-literal process-spawn call to the probe
classification_rationale: both spawn queries match agents/plugins/[^/]+/src/.*; neither header contains a spawn token today, the lexical gate (check-plugin-spawn-lexical.sh) scans agents/shared, and CodeQL is scheduled rather than required
summary: The CodeQL spawn queries no longer cover the moved code. Deferred to the same new issue as the README-touch rule: widen both regexps to include agents/shared/.
